clue.text: Rough clubs like strong-flavoured alcohol

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a beer heavy with hops tastes hoppy

explanation.surface: A golfer or drinker remarks on clubs that resemble a powerful, bitter drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough water is choppy, broken into short irregular waves.

clue.text: Kind of parable in which tiger perhaps drives all away

indicators.note: the feline drives out the other piece, taking its place
away completes the sense of being driven off and replaced

parts.note: an allegory is a parable or symbolic tale
taken as written
a tiger is an example of a big cat

explanation.surface: A sort of fable in which a tiger chases off everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' is the definition, a noun meaning sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A category is a class or sort of things sharing features.

clue.text: Postholder's inaccurate figures perhaps shown up by actuary's conclusion

parts.note: out means wrong, as in a guess being out

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means the letters run upwards, reversed

parts.note: figures such as statues are art

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An office holder's wrong numbers are exposed by the actuary's verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Postholder' suggests a holder of a job, but is a tray holding mail.
explanation.definitionFit: An out-tray is a tray on a desk holding outgoing mail and documents.

clue.text: In report, insurance company released correct text

indicators.note: in report means as heard, so the spoken words are respelt

parts.note: the Pru, the Prudential insurer, is freed

explanation.surface: A news report says an insurer was let off, which corrects a text.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pru is the Prudential, a well-known British insurance company.
explanation.definitionFit: To proofread is to check and mark errors in written copy before printing.

clue.text: Cockney's unexciting, simple …

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker famously turns a TH sound into F, so the phrase is said in that accent

parts.note: something unexciting offers no thrills

explanation.surface: A Londoner calls something dull and plain, with the ellipsis running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney's' governs the sound: a Cockney says 'no thrills' with an F for the TH. Cockney is the working-class accent of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something basic, without extras or ornament, is described as plain or no-frills.

clue.text: Striking astronauts fired here

definitions.meaning: astronauts are launched off the planet, beyond Earth

explanation.surface: Striking astronauts have been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests sacking and 'Striking' suggests industrial action; really they are launched into space.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wonderful or extraordinary is described informally as beyond earthly.

clue.text: Governor's measure applied in school?

definitions.meaning: a measuring stick once applied to pupils' knuckles as punishment

explanation.surface: A school governor's disciplinary measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applied' hints at old-fashioned corporal punishment with the rule.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sovereign and a straight measuring stick.

clue.text: A gumboil requiring treatment, I must avoid pain

indicators.note: something requiring treatment is in bad shape, so these letters are rearranged
the letter must be left out of the mix, avoided

explanation.surface: A mouth abscess needs medical attention, and the patient must stay clear of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from the letters of A GUMBOIL and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the muscles of the lower back.

clue.text: Something loose on hillside attended by northern vet

parts.note: scree is loose stone covering a slope

explanation.surface: A vet from the north tends to an animal loose on a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vet' looks like an animal doctor but is the verb meaning check.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet someone is to check or examine them thoroughly.

clue.text: Keep fitter? Do — it gives poorly folk a pick-up

definitions.text: it gives poorly folk a pick-up

parts.note: someone stretching to stay fit is whimsically a stretcher
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An exercise class organiser invites everyone to a social to cheer the sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick-up' suggests cheering up, but means literally lifting the sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A team of bearers carrying sick or injured people on a litter lifts them up.

clue.text: … pork-pie maybe gives satisfaction

definitions.meaning: a pork-pie is a style of hat, and in Cockney rhyming slang (carried over from the previous clue) a hat is a '...'
retaliation in kind, getting even, as when one demands satisfaction

explanation.surface: Continuing the Cockney's speech: a pork pie gives contentment.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 'Cockney's' in 4 Across, signalling rhyming slang: a pork-pie hat rhymes as 'tit for tat'. Rhyming slang replaces a word with a phrase that rhymes with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving tit for tat is repaying an injury in kind, which is a form of getting satisfaction.

clue.text: Social climber brings back unusual article from Spain

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it, so the assembled pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: rum means odd or unusual
el is the Spanish definite article

explanation.surface: An ambitious socialite returns from Spain with a strange item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social climber' looks like a snob, but means a gregarious tree-climbing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are sociable primates living in groups and climbing trees in Madagascar.

clue.text: Being looked up to by others

definitions.text: Being looked up to by others

parts.words: Being looked up to by others
parts.note: sounds like an admired person, but literally describes the tallest of creatures, which others must look upwards to see

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys the respect of those around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a noun (a creature), and 'looked up to' is literal rather than meaning admired.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-necked African animal is the tallest living creature, so all others gaze upward at it.

clue.text: Criminal's piercing cry when driving, banned

indicators.note: one piece piercing another goes right into it, so these letters sit inside the golf shout

parts.note: golfers shout fore when driving a ball towards others
bad can mean wicked or criminal

explanation.surface: A criminal's shrill shout while at the wheel gets him barred from the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving' suggests a car but refers to hitting a golf ball off the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbade is the past tense of forbid, so it means prohibited or barred.

clue.text: Frost said something read

indicators.note: said signals that a word is spoken, so the spelling shifts to one that sounds the same

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: The poet Robert Frost spoke something that was read out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' looks like the poet, apt for verse, but is the ice crystals.
explanation.definitionFit: A verse or poem in rhyme is something that people read.

clue.text: Sticking together with the man breaking up company racket, shortly to retire

indicators.note: the pronoun breaks up the following letters by going between them
to retire is to go back, so these letters are read backwards
shortly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a racket is a din, noise
he is the pronoun for the man

explanation.surface: A man disrupting a firm's crooked scheme soon to stand down shows solidarity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims the din by its last letter and 'to retire' turns the rest back; 'breaking up' puts the pronoun between the firm and that.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohesion is the act or state of particles or people holding firmly together.

clue.text: Aqueous kind, I've rage to submerge

definitions.text: Aqueous kind, I've rage to submerge

indicators.note: the answer is submerged within these words, spanning them

explanation.surface: A watery type declares a passion for going under.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a water-loving type with an urge to dive below the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver who swims underwater without a suit is a watery type keen to go down.

clue.text: Banquet's beginning with exotic taster — butterscotch at heart

indicators.note: exotic means unusual or foreign, so these letters are rearranged
the heart of a word is its central letters

explanation.surface: A feast opens with a foreign food critic and butterscotch in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges TASTER to STARTE; the middle letters of butterscotch give RS.
explanation.definitionFit: Starters are the first courses, the opening dishes of a meal.

clue.text: Drought as school subject? In retrospect, aim to get dope about that

indicators.note: the fool's letters go about, around, the rest

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
RI is religious instruction, a school subject

indicators.note: looking in retrospect is looking back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether drought could be taught at school, then plans to buy drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: RI (religious instruction) is a British school subject. 'In retrospect' turns the aim back, and 'about' wraps the fool round it all; 'dope' suggests drugs, but is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Drought is a prolonged lack of rain, so dryness of land is the condition described.

clue.text: Something to eat from barbecue's ending with stock jam topping

indicators.note: in a down clue, topping places one piece above the rest

parts.note: to ram is to jam or cram

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

parts.note: kin means family, stock, lineage

explanation.surface: A barbecue dish finishes with a jam made from stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' looks like a preserve but is the verb to cram.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramekin is a small dish from which food is eaten, often baked individual portions.

clue.text: Mug incorporates motto I'd invented, contrarily? On the contrary

indicators.note: contrarily means the other way round, so the found letters are read backwards
the letters needed are incorporated within the run of words, spanning them

explanation.surface: A cup bears a slogan someone made up to be contrary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the container: the words incorporate the answer, not the mug the words; 'contrarily' reverses the letters found.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug is slang for a fool, someone gullible and easily duped.

clue.text: Concentrated, as the decimal system is initially easy to follow

indicators.note: to follow puts the letter after the preceding piece

parts.note: the decimal system counts in tens

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter

explanation.surface: Decimal arithmetic is easy to follow if you concentrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means highly focused or strong, as a concentrated flavour is.

clue.text: Resentment of the more experienced English is evident in meeting

indicators.note: being evident in something means being visible inside it

parts.note: an AGM is an annual general meeting
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bitterness towards senior staff comes out at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageism is prejudice against older people, discrimination on grounds of years.

clue.text: Good beer this person's spilled over old girl's uniform

indicators.note: something spilled over is tipped over, so the letters are turned backwards

parts.note: Pils is a pale lager, short for Pilsner
the setter refers to self, so this person's means my

explanation.surface: Someone knocked their good beer over a former pupil's school uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old girl' suggests an elderly woman but means a former schoolgirl. A gymslip is a sleeveless tunic worn in British girls' schools.
explanation.definitionFit: This pinafore dress was a standard part of uniform for British schoolgirls in the past.

clue.text: Extremely uplifting wearing cap — swimmers like them

parts.note: a cap is a lid, worn on top; here it sits above the rest of this down entry

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting raises the letters, reversing them

parts.note: so means very, extremely

explanation.surface: Swimmers find wearing a swim cap greatly encouraging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns SO upwards beneath LID in this down entry. A lido is an open-air public swimming pool, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lidos are outdoor pools, which bathers enjoy.

clue.text: One aged fifty, in taking too many pills, gets disturbed rest

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the abbreviation for an overdose

parts.note: OD means overdose
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: disturbed means put in disarray, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A man of fifty overdoes the medication and sleeps badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' shuffles REST to STER.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldster is an informal word for an elderly person.

clue.text: Cut by point of knife, one bloodied makes wound up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: these letters are cut into by the knife's tip, which goes inside

parts.note: bloodied means red

indicators.note: the point of a word is its leading letter

explanation.surface: Someone stabbed with a knife and left bloody ends up badly hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound up' looks like the noun wound, but means annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be wound up is to be irritated or annoyed, the same as irritated.

clue.text: Appropriateness of English verb seized upon by sacked cleaner

indicators.note: these abbreviations are held inside the shuffled letters
sacked suggests wreckage, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: V is the grammatical abbreviation for verb

explanation.surface: A dismissed cleaner grabs on to the suitability of an English verb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' rearranges CLEANER into RELANCE, and EV goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevance is pertinence, how fitting or apt something is to the matter in hand.

clue.text: Takes care of survey — memory's required

parts.note: minds means looks after
to eye is to look over or survey

explanation.surface: Someone who looks after surveying needs to be able to remember.
explanation.definitionFit: The mind's eye is the faculty of picturing things, including remembered scenes, in imagination.

clue.text: Instructions by which privates will be constrained

definitions.meaning: briefings given to a lawyer or team, orders

definitions.text: by which privates will be constrained
definitions.meaning: underpants hold in the private parts

explanation.surface: Orders constraining army privates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'privates' suggests soldiers, but means the genitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs are both a set of instructions and close-fitting underpants.
